newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end soft ahead of long weekend.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end soft ahead of long weekend.

text.p: Argentina's bolsa closed marginally lower Friday as players locked in profits ahead of a long weekend break, dealers said.
But stocks were seen firm when trading resumes Tuesday.

"Stocks carried out a very healthy correction today," said Gabriel Ruiz at brokers Tavelli. "We have to allow for some selling at this stage of gains, which allows the market to recover its strength and aim higher again."
The blue-chip MerVal index dipped 0.1 percent to 813.40. It closed up 1.3 percent on the week and stands 4.3 percent higher so far in June.

"The market is playing catch-up to economic indicators," Tavelli said, noting recent data on growth topped consensus estimates and forced analysts to revise their forecasts. "The economy has grown 12 percent in the past four quarters and we expect a GDP rise this year of at least 8.0 percent."
Floor volume eased to 36.1 million pesos from 39.5 million Thursday, while over-the-counter turnover shrank to 83.6 million pesos from 96.9 million Thursday.
The broad market index matched MerVal losses of 0.1 percent, but winning issues still bashed losers 43 to 22 and 17 stocks closed flat.
Top main-tier performers were holding company Garovaglio, electricity generator Central Costanera and foods giant Molinos, which tacked on 3.1 percent, 2.3 percent and 1.3 percent, respectively.

The sharpest MerVal loser was carmaker Sevel, which fell 3.7 percent after the Securities Commission late Thursday said it began a formal probe into alleged price manipulation by the company in a 1992 share offer. Sevel has denied the charges.
Other strong losers were steelmaker Acindar and Telecom, both off 2.2 percent.
